messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High tenant eviction rate observed for customer-579 in dedicated-pool-eu-west-1. Impact: request failures and 503s for pinned VPC endpoints. Paging on-call @maya and @jonah :rotating_light:

maya: On it. Jumping in — can someone paste the initial alert details?

jonah: I'm on commute but available. Pulling metrics now.

ops-runner: Alert payload: eviction_rate=0.14 (baseline 0.001), evictions_per_min=850, affected_instances=11/24. Affected route prefix: /v1/infer/customer-579/*

eli: Possible cause: scheduler restarted nodes during rolling upgrade earlier this morning. I saw a partial config push to dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 at 06:12UTC with new routing policy.

luis: Adding context: customer-579 uses Dedicated + VPC. Their tenant mapping is strict. Evictions mean tenant sessions are being forcibly removed from pinned workers, leading to 503s.

rachel: @maya can we confirm whether eviction is happening because of tenant ID collisions (wrong prefix) or because of kernel OOM on the worker?

maya: Triage plan: 1) Stop further scheduling changes. 2) Isolate an affected worker and dump routing table and container logs. 3) Temporarily route customer-579 traffic to warm fallback pool while we investigate. 4) Notify customer ops.

alice-customer: Thanks for the heads-up. We're seeing errors start around 06:20UTC — some of our requests return 503 with body: "session eviction: tenant mismatch". We're holding traffic on our side if you need us to.

jonah: Quick check: querying runtime routing for one affected worker (worker-id: wp-7682):
```
$ rwctl inspect worker wp-7682 --show-routing
worker: wp-7682
model-routes:
  /v1/infer/customer-578 -> bucket A
  /v1/infer/customer-579 -> bucket B
  /v1/infer/customer-579 -> bucket C  # duplicate entry
backend-pinned-tenants: customer-579
kv-cache-size: 12GB
last-restart: 2024-10-05T06:11:12Z
```
jonah: There's a duplicate route entry for customer-579 pointing to two buckets; that smells like a config merge issue leading to double-assignments and eviction when locks conflict.

eli: I can confirm recent config push included a stale partial of an old rollout. Seems the rollout reconcile job retried halfway and created duplicate route manifests for the same tenant.

maya: Actioning immediate mitigations: 1) Prevent further reconcile runs for the pool. 2) Run a one-off dedupe on routing manifests for dedicated-pool-eu-west-1. 3) Warm fallback route to dedicated-warm-eu-west-1 and update smart-routing policy to route customer-579 to warm pool only.

ops-runner: Executing commands now:
```
$ orchestrator pause-reconcile --pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 --reason "incident-1840123456"
PAUSED: reconcile job paused for pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-1

$ orchestrator dedupe-routes --pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 --tenant customer-579 --dry-run
DRY-RUN: 3 duplicate manifests detected for tenant customer-579

$ orchestrator dedupe-routes --pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 --tenant customer-579 --apply
APPLY: removed 2 duplicate manifests, canonicalized route -> bucket B
```

luis: After dedupe, starting a controlled eviction fix to rebind sessions without mass disconnects: replacing pinned assignment for customer-579 on affected nodes with graceful handoff.

rachel: I'm updating routing rules in the control plane to pin customer-579 to dedicated-warm-eu-west-1 with immediate fallback priority.

ops-runner: Routing update diff:
```
- smart-routing(customer-579): [primary: dedicated-pool-eu-west-1, fallback: dedicated-warm-eu-west-1]
+ smart-routing(customer-579): [primary: dedicated-warm-eu-west-1, fallback: dedicated-pool-eu-west-1]
```
ops-runner: Policy applied. Confirming traffic shift metrics.

jonah: Metrics after shift (2m window): error_rate down from 12% -> 1.3%, request latency stable. Evictions_per_min reduced to 12.

maya: Great. Notify customer with mitigation details and ETA for full restore.

maya: @alice-customer we've routed your traffic to a warm pool to stop evictions while we finish cleanup. No data crossed tenants; this was a routing manifest duplication issue causing conflict-based evictions. We're continuing to reconcile and will report once original pool is safe.

alice-customer: Appreciate the quick action. Please confirm when we can resume normal routing — we prefer the original pool for capacity reasons.

eli: Next steps: 1) Run a full audit of reconcile logs to find the rollout that produced duplicates. 2) Harden reconcile so duplicates are rejected. 3) Run a tenant isolation check across all pools for similar duplicate-manifest patterns.

luis: I'll take the audit and follow up with PR to avoid partial commit on retries.

rachel: Ops, plan for gradual migration back: verify no duplicates for 30m, then shift routing priority back with canary on 2 nodes, observe 10m, then expand.

ops-runner: Scheduling canary cutover in 20 minutes. Will post results.

jonah: Remote logs from the problematic workers show no cross-tenant traffic in the traces. Verified by tracing-id sample: trace-0a3b4c.

maya: Incident status: Mitigated (traffic shifted). On-call handoff: @jonah will own overnight for monitoring; @luis will own the reconcile PR; @rachel will run the migration plan; I'll handle customer comms.

jonah: Acknowledged. I'll keep an eye on evictions and error budget metrics.

ops-runner: Canary results (10m): 0 evictions, error_rate 0.2%, latency unchanged. Proceeding with staged rollout.

maya: Closing incident channel when all stages complete and customer sign-off. Thanks team. :pray:
